* `closed` - CLOSED
* `merged` - MERGED

is_draft.description: True if the pull request is a draft.

created_at.description: When the pull request was opened.

merged_at.description: When the pull request was merged, or null.

open_to_merge_seconds.description: Coarse open-to-merge time in seconds (merged_at - created_at; fuses draft and ready-for-review time). Null until merged.

ready_to_merge_seconds.description: True ready-to-merge cycle time in seconds: merged_at minus the last observed ready_for_review transition (only the last draft/ready switch counts), or minus created_at for a merged PR verifiably never drafted. Null when unmerged or not observed (the PR's life isn't fully inside the synced issue-event window) - null never means zero.

labels.description: GitHub label names on the pull request.

pushes.description: CI triggers attributed to this PR: distinct head SHAs across its workflow runs. Fork-PR runs are unattributed.

rerun_cycles.description: Workflow runs attributed to this PR that were a 2nd+ attempt (a re-run).

estimated_cost_usd.description: Estimated CI cost in USD summed over this PR's jobs (billable runners only). Null when nothing was costable or the job-level source isn't synced.

billable_minutes.description: Billable (self-hosted) minutes summed over this PR's jobs. Null when the job source isn't synced.

ready_to_merge_seconds.description: Seconds from the last ready_for_review to merge. Null when not observed.

ready_to_first_approval_seconds.description: Seconds from ready to the first approval. Null without an approval or review data.

first_approval_to_merge_seconds.description: Seconds from the first approval to merge. Null without an approval or review data.

before_first_approval_share.description: Share (0 to 1) of the ready-to-merge time spent before the first approval.

PullRequestReviewCommentCreate.description:
Request body for posting an inline PR review comment as the requesting user.

Two shapes: a reply to an existing thread (only `body` + `in_reply_to`), or a new
thread on a diff line (`body` + `path` + `line`, optionally `side`).

in_reply_to.description: Numeric id of the thread root comment to reply to. When set, path/line/side are ignored.

path.description: File path to anchor a new comment thread to (required when starting a new thread).

line.description: Diff line to anchor a new comment thread to (required when starting a new thread).

side.description:
Diff side of the anchor line: 'LEFT' = deletions, 'RIGHT' = additions. Defaults to 'RIGHT'.

* `LEFT` - LEFT
* `RIGHT` - RIGHT

PullRequestReviewCommentCreateResponse.description: Response after posting a review comment — the created comment in the normalized PR-comment shape.

PullRequestReviewCommentReactionCreate.description: Request body for adding an emoji reaction to a review comment.

Reaction to add: one of '+1', '-1', 'laugh', 'hooray', 'confused', 'heart', 'rocket', 'eyes'.

* `+1` - +1
* `-1` - -1
* `laugh` - laugh
* `hooray` - hooray
* `confused` - confused
* `heart` - heart
* `rocket` - rocket
* `eyes` - eyes

reason.description: Why the test was quarantined.

added.description: ISO date the entry was added.

expires.description: ISO date the quarantine expires; past it the test blocks CI normally again.

'run' (the test still executes but cannot fail the suite) or 'skip' (not run at all).

* `run` - RUN
* `skip` - SKIP

lifecycle.description:
Expiry classification: 'active' (>7 days left), 'expiring_soon' (0-7 days left), 'in_grace' (expired up to 7 days ago), 'overdue' (expired beyond the grace period).

* `active` - ACTIVE
* `expiring_soon` - EXPIRING_SOON
* `in_grace` - IN_GRACE
* `overdue` - OVERDUE

days_until_expiry.description: Days until the entry expires; negative once past expiry.

selector_kind.description:

* `product` - PRODUCT
* `file` - FILE
* `directory` - DIRECTORY
* `test` - TEST

entries.description: Quarantined selectors, most urgent first (overdue, in_grace, expiring_soon, active), then by soonest expiry.

repo.description: Repository the file was read from. Null in local-dev mode, where the server's own checkout is read.

available.description: False when the repository has no quarantine file (not an error) or it could not be fetched.

parse_errors.description: Contract violations (malformed JSON, bad entries) or fetch failures. Malformed entries are dropped; well-formed ones are kept.

parse_warnings.description: Forward-compatibility notices, e.g. unknown entry fields.

source_url.description: GitHub blob URL of the quarantine file, or empty when read locally or unavailable.

generated_at.description: When this snapshot was computed (UTC); expiry math uses this clock.

reason.description: Why this snapshot is being quarantined.

expires_at.description: When the quarantine lifts itself, as an ISO 8601 datetime. Through MCP an omitted or later expiry becomes 30 days from now; anywhere else omitting it means no expiry.

source_run_id.description: Optional pointer to the run whose failing snapshot prompted this quarantine — used to surface a 'view the failing run' link later.

notify_owners.description: Post the quarantine to the Slack channel of the team that owns the story, naming the user who quarantined it. Only Storybook snapshots have an owning team. Best effort: skipped when the story has no owning team or the project has no Slack integration.

id.description: UUID of the lift request.

quarantine_id.description: UUID of the quarantine event this request lifts. A later quarantine of the same snapshot is a different event.

run_type.description: Run type of the quarantine, for example storybook.

pr_number.description: Pull request whose merge the lift waits for.

expected_hash.description: Content hash a default-branch run must render, against a baseline entry with the same hash, for the lift to apply.

state.description:
`pending` waits for the merge and a matching default-branch run. `applied` lifted the quarantine. `cancelled` was withdrawn, or the pull request closed without merging into the run's branch. `superseded` means the quarantine ended some other way, or another request lifted it.

* `pending` - pending
* `applied` - applied
* `cancelled` - cancelled
* `superseded` - superseded

detail.description: The latest verification outcome, in plain words.

updated_at.description: When the request last changed.

resolved_at.description: When the request left `pending`. Null while it waits.

source_run_id.description: Run the lift was requested from. Null after that run is deleted.

requested_by.description: User who requested the lift, or on whose behalf an agent did.

merge_commit_sha.description: Merge commit of the pull request. Set when the lift applies.

lifted_at_sha.description: Commit of the default-branch run that proved the fix and lifted the quarantine. A branch that does not contain it still treats the snapshot as quarantined.

source.description: Who requested the lift: `human` for a person in the UI, `agent` for an agent through MCP.

operation.description:
What to do: 'quarantine' (add or replace an entry and file a tracking issue), 'extend' (re-stamp an existing entry's expiry, reusing its issue), or 'remove' (delete the entry). All three open a pull request.

* `quarantine` - QUARANTINE
* `extend` - EXTEND
* `remove` - REMOVE

selector.description: Test selector to act on: an exact test id, a file, a directory, a class prefix, or 'product:<dashed-name>'.

runner.description:
Test runner the selector targets: 'pytest', 'jest', or 'playwright'. Existing entries and Jest file extensions are inferred for older clients that omit it; other selectors default to 'pytest'.

* `pytest` - PYTEST
* `jest` - JEST
* `playwright` - PLAYWRIGHT

repo.description: Optional 'owner/name' repository override; defaults to the team's most active repo.

reason.description: Why the test is quarantined. Required for quarantine and extend; ignored by remove.

owner.description: GitHub team or user handle responsible for the fix, e.g. '@PostHog/team-x'. Required for quarantine and extend.

issue.description: Existing tracking issue URL, carried forward on extend and remove. Ignored by quarantine, which files a fresh issue.

expires.description: ISO date the quarantine expires (at most 30 days out). Defaults to 14 days from today. Ignored by remove.

mode.description:
'run' (the test still executes but cannot fail the suite) or 'skip' (not run at all). Defaults to 'run'.

* `run` - RUN
* `skip` - SKIP

pr_url.description: URL of the opened pull request that edits the quarantine file.

issue_url.description: URL of the tracking issue filed for a new quarantine; empty for extend and remove.

branch.description: Branch the pull request was opened from.

source_run.description: Run whose failing snapshot prompted this quarantine. Null when quarantine was created without run context.

name.description: Name of the query, preferably unique. For example web_analytics_vitals
name.title: Name

productKey.title: Productkey

scene.description: Scene where this query is shown in the UI. Use string, there's no need to churn the Schema when we add a new Scene *

query.description:
Submit a JSON string representing a query for PostHog data analysis, for example a HogQL query.

Example payload:

```

{"query": {"kind": "HogQLQuery", "query": "select * from events limit 100"}}

```

For more details on HogQL queries, see the [PostHog HogQL documentation](/docs/hogql#api-access).
query.title: Query

refresh.description:
Whether results should be calculated sync or async, and how much to rely on the cache:
- `'blocking'` - calculate synchronously (returning only when the query is done), UNLESS there are very fresh results in the cache
- `'async'` - kick off background calculation (returning immediately with a query status), UNLESS there are very fresh results in the cache
- `'lazy_async'` - kick off background calculation, UNLESS there are somewhat fresh results in the cache
- `'force_blocking'` - calculate synchronously, even if fresh results are already cached
- `'force_async'` - kick off background calculation, even if fresh results are already cached
- `'force_cache'` - return cached data or a cache miss; always completes immediately as it never calculates Background calculation can be tracked using the `query_status` response field.

RecordCheckResultRequest.description: Request body for `scout-check-record-result`: the verdict on one dispatched report check.

check_id.description: The check this run was dispatched to answer, as given in the run note.

outcome.description:
`passed` when the evidence meets the check's stated bar and the expectation holds, `failed` when the evidence meets the bar and the expectation does not hold. `inconclusive` when your tools worked but the evidence cannot settle the question; give a `reason`. `errored` only when a tool, query, or model call failed. `failed` retires the check, so use it for a conclusion, not a suspicion.

* `passed` - Passed
* `failed` - Failed
* `errored` - Errored
* `inconclusive` - Inconclusive

reason.description:
Required with `inconclusive`, and refused with any other outcome. `awaiting_data`: the data can still arrive (a rollout lag, a soak not complete, too few samples so far), so the check looks again later. `unmeasurable`: the data the check needs is not captured. `needs_manual_verification`: only a person or another environment can verify it. `no_fix_to_measure`: nothing was changed to fix the claim, so no window after a fix exists. A report resolved without a pull request still has a window that starts when it resolved. Every reason except `awaiting_data` ends the check.

* `awaiting_data` - Awaiting Data
* `unmeasurable` - Unmeasurable
* `needs_manual_verification` - Needs Manual Verification
* `no_fix_to_measure` - No Fix To Measure

Best-effort — a `run_id` that is unparseable, or that isn't a run on this project, is dropped rather than rejected, so the memory write is never lost. Omit it and the lineage still lands: a write from a scout sandbox is attributed to that sandbox's own run.

expires_at.description: Optional ISO-8601 expiry for a memory that's only true for a while (a cooldown, a window you're watching). After this time the entry drops out of searches, so you don't have to come back and forget it. Omit for a durable memory — every write sets the whole entry, so omitting it on a later write clears an expiry set earlier. Best-effort — a value that can't be parsed or is already in the past is dropped (the memory stays durable), not rejected, so the memory write is never lost.

* `monthly` - Monthly
* `yearly` - Yearly

* `two_column` - two_column
* `three_column` - three_column
* `full_width` - full_width

Where the producing scanner came from. `configured` scanners are saved, named, and have a detail page; `inline` ones are throwaways minted for a one-off scan and are not addressable, so callers must not link to them.

* `configured` - Configured
* `inline` - Inline

session_id.description: Session recording id this scanner was applied to.

status.description:
Observation status (pending, running, succeeded, failed, ineligible).

* `pending` - Pending
* `running` - Running
* `succeeded` - Succeeded
* `failed` - Failed
* `ineligible` - Ineligible

error_reason.description: Populated on terminal non-success statuses; formatted as `kind:human-readable message`. For `ineligible`, kind is one of no_recording / too_short / too_inactive / too_long / no_events / no_snapshots / too_large / not_exposed / experiment_unresolved. For `failed`, kind is one of provider_transient / provider_rejected / rasterization_failed / validation_failed / infra_transient / internal_error / orphaned / pii_detected.

workflow_id.description: Temporal workflow id for progress queries and debugging. Empty until the workflow starts.

scanner_snapshot.description: Frozen view of the scanner at run time; scanner edits do not retroactively mutate this observation.

scanner_result.description: Result data persisted on success; null until the observation succeeds.

prompt_question.description: The scanner's prompt condensed into the one question it answers about a session. Null when the prompt has changed since this observation was scanned, since the question then describes a different prompt; read `scanner_snapshot.scanner_config.prompt` instead.

triggered_by.description:
Whether this observation came from the schedule, an on-demand request, a retry of a failed or ineligible observation, or a historical backfill.

* `schedule` - Schedule
* `on_demand` - On demand
* `retry` - Retry
* `backfill` - Backfill

triggered_by_user.description: User who triggered an on-demand observation; null for scheduled observations.

backfill_id.description: Backfill that dispatched this observation; null for live, on-demand, and retry triggers.

distinct_id.description: Distinct id of the person in the recorded session (the subject being watched); null if unknown.

recording_subject_email.description: Email of the person in the recorded session (the subject being watched, not the user who triggered the observation), captured at scan time. Null when the session had no identified person.

previous_observation_id.description: Id of the preceding sibling observation for the same scanner (prev/next nav), honoring any list filters and ordering passed to retrieve; only set on retrieve, null at the start of the set.

next_observation_id.description: Id of the following sibling observation for the same scanner (prev/next nav), honoring any list filters and ordering passed to retrieve; only set on retrieve, null at the end of the set.

label.description: The team's shared label on this observation (correct/incorrect + feedback), or null if unlabeled.

viewed.description: Whether the calling user has opened this observation.

media.description: Thumbnails and clips illustrating this observation, in order. Empty until the media render finishes.

summary_line.description: One line of plain text saying what the scanner found: its verdict, score, tags or title, then its own words, with markdown flattened and the text truncated. An observation that produced no result carries the reason instead, and one still in flight carries an empty string. Read this in place of `scanner_result` when you scan a list of observations.

ReplayObservationLabel.description: The team's shared judgement on whether the scanner scored this session correctly.

is_correct.description: True if the scanner scored this session correctly, false if not.

feedback.description: Optional written context on the rating, for thumbs-up and thumbs-down alike: what the scanner got right or wrong, or what it should have concluded.

ReplayObservationMedia.description: One thumbnail or clip illustrating an observation.

id.description: Id of this media entry.

kind.description:
`thumbnail` for the single frame that illustrates the observation, `chapter` for the frame of one summary chapter, `clip` for a short video.

* `thumbnail` - Thumbnail
* `clip` - Clip
* `chapter` - Chapter

position.description: Order among media of the same kind. For a `chapter` frame, the index into `model_output.chapters`.

asset_id.description: Export asset holding the bytes; fetch it from the export content endpoint.

description.description: One sentence saying what the clip shows. Null for thumbnails.

video_start_ms.description: Where this media starts in the analysis video, in milliseconds.

video_end_ms.description: Where a clip ends in the analysis video, in milliseconds. Null for thumbnails.

ReplayScanner.description: A Replay Vision scanner: its type, targeting query, and AI configuration.

name.description: Human-readable scanner name. Unique within the team.

description.description: Free-form description shown in the scanner management UI.

tags.description: Organizational tags for this scanner. Distinct from a classifier's categories in scanner_config. Tags cannot contain commas.

scanner_type.description:
What the scanner does: monitor, classifier, scorer, or summarizer.

* `monitor` - Monitor
* `classifier` - Classifier
* `scorer` - Scorer
* `summarizer` - Summarizer
* `experiment` - Experiment

goal.description: The goal an AI draft was built from, in the creator's own words, so the scanner keeps what it was meant to find. Set on create only and ignored on update.

creation_method.description:
How the creator built this scanner: from an AI draft, from a template, or from scratch. Reported to product analytics at creation and not stored on the scanner. Independent of any experiment the creator is in, since a person offered the AI flow can still fill the form by hand. Only the app can answer this, so a request from anywhere else reports the calling surface instead of whatever it sends here. Ignored on update.

* `ai` - AI draft
* `template` - Template
* `scratch` - From scratch

scanner_config.description: Type-specific configuration. All scanner types require `prompt`; monitors add optional `allow_inconclusive`, classifiers add `tags`, scorers add `scale`, summarizers add optional `length`.

prompt_question.description: The current prompt condensed by AI into the one question the scanner answers about a session. Falls back to the prompt's first line when no question matches the current prompt.

query.description: Persisted `RecordingsQuery` shape used to pick candidate sessions. `date_from`/`date_to` are stripped on save — the schedule controls time, not the user.

sampling_rate.description: 0..1 random downsample applied after the query matches. Defaults to 1.0 (no downsampling). Use exactly 0 to pause scanning; non-zero rates below 0.0001 (0.01%) are rejected as below the sampling precision.

sampling_mode.description:
Quality pre-filter applied before random sampling. focused = top sessions only, balanced = drops the lowest-quality, comprehensive = no filter (default).

* `focused` - Focused
* `balanced` - Balanced
* `comprehensive` - Comprehensive

credit_limit.description: Optional cap on this scanner's own credit spend per billing period. Null means no scanner-level cap. When reached, this scanner stops scanning until the period resets. It stays enabled and does not scan the sessions it skipped.

provider.description:
LLM provider. v1 is Google-only.

* `google` - Google

model.description:
Concrete model to use for this scanner.

* `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` - Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite
* `gemini-3-flash-preview` - Gemini 3 Flash
* `gemini-3.8-flash` - Gemini 3.8 Flash

enabled.description: When false, the reconciler removes the scanner's Temporal schedule. On-demand triggers still work.

emits_signals.description: When true, the prompt is augmented with the Signal side mission and the scanner emits PostHog Signals.

experiment_targeting.description: The experiment this scanner's targeting watches, if any. Set null when the experiment targeting is removed.

scanner_version.description: Increments on every config-changing save. Observations snapshot this value.

estimated_monthly_observations.description: Latest projected observations/month for this scanner. Null until first computed.

estimated_at.description: When `estimated_monthly_observations` was last computed. Null means the estimate is being recomputed after a config change or has never run, so the stored number may be stale.

credits_per_observation.description: Credits one observation by this scanner costs (1 credit = $0.01), derived from `model`.

estimated_monthly_credits.description: `estimated_monthly_observations` priced at `credits_per_observation`, capped at `credit_limit` when one is set. Null until the estimate is first computed.

credits_this_month.description: Credits this scanner's succeeded observations consumed in the current billing period (1 credit = $0.01). Matches the window of the org-wide quota meter.

observations_this_month.description: Succeeded observations this scanner produced in the current billing period.

credits_used_against_limit.description: Credits counted against `credit_limit` for the current billing period: settled receipts plus in-flight observations, priced from their frozen snapshot model. This is what the limit gate measures, so it includes work still in progress. It is not the same as `credits_this_month`, which counts only succeeded observations.

limit_reached.description: Whether this scanner has stopped because of its own credit limit. True when `credit_limit` is set and the budget left cannot cover one more observation, which is the same test the scanner's enforcement gates apply. Always false when no limit is set.

sweep_throttle_factor.description: How much the scheduled sweep is slowed to keep this scanner inside its daily ClickHouse read budget. 1 means it checks for new recordings on the normal schedule; N means it checks once every N schedule intervals. Expensive filters raise it.

last_swept_at.description: Watermark for the scanner's last scheduled fire. Mirrors Temporal schedule state for recovery.

created_by.description: User who created the scanner.

user_access_level.description: The effective access level the user has for this object

window_start.description: Inclusive lower bound of the historical window to scan.

window_end.description: Exclusive upper bound of the window; clamped to now at creation.

total_count.description: Unobserved candidates enumerated at creation; the ceiling is total_count x credits_per_observation.

skipped_count.description: Candidates the walk stepped over because this scanner had already tried them. Counted at creation but never dispatched, so progress and remaining spend both have to account for them.

credits_per_observation.description: Per-observation credit price frozen at creation from the snapshot model.

succeeded_count.description: Observations from this backfill that succeeded.

failed_count.description: Observations from this backfill that failed.

ineligible_count.description: Sessions that turned out ineligible (too short, expired recording, ...).

in_flight_count.description: Observations from this backfill still pending or running.

finished_at.description: When the backfill reached a terminal status (completed or cancelled).

ReplayVisionError.description: The shape every Replay Vision error response uses, so generated clients read one key.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation of why the request was refused.

cost_series.description: CI cost per merged PR across the window, oldest first, zero-filled, bucketed by cost_series_granularity. Empty when the job-level source isn't synced or include_series=false.

time_to_green_series.description: Median time-to-green (p50 wall clock for a PR push round to settle fully green) per bucket across the window, oldest first, bucketed by time_to_green_series_granularity. Empty buckets carry null; the whole series is empty when include_series=false.

success_rate_series.description: CI pass rate (conclusive runs that succeeded, all branches) per bucket across the window, oldest first, bucketed by success_rate_series_granularity. Skipped, cancelled, neutral, and action_required runs are excluded. Empty buckets carry null; the whole series is empty when include_series=false.

open_to_merge_series.description: Median time-to-merge (p50 open_to_merge_seconds, bots/drafts excluded) per bucket across the window, oldest first, bucketed by open_to_merge_series_granularity. Empty buckets carry null; the whole series is empty when include_series=false.

delivery_pipeline.description: Where a change's wall-clock time goes on the way to production, over PRs merged in the window with bots and drafts excluded.

ready_to_merge_series.description: Median cycle time (p50 per-PR ready_to_merge_seconds, bots/drafts excluded) per bucket across the window, oldest first, bucketed by ready_to_merge_series_granularity. Empty buckets carry null; the whole series is empty when the issue-events table isn't synced or include_series=false, so fall back to open_to_merge_series.

run_count.description: Workflow runs started in the window, all branches and workflows.

run_count_prev.description: Same count over the equal-length window immediately before date_from: the delta baseline.

success_rate.description: Fraction of conclusive runs that succeeded (0-1) in the window. Skipped, cancelled, neutral, and action_required runs are excluded. Null if no run reached a verdict.

success_rate_prev.description: Conclusive-run success rate over the previous window. Null if no run reached a verdict.

rerun_cycles.description: Runs in the window that were a 2nd+ attempt (attempt > 1).

rerun_cycles_prev.description: Re-run cycles over the previous window.

merged_pr_count.description: PRs merged in the window, all authors and bots included. billable_minutes and estimated_cost_usd cover every run in the window, including default-branch and unmerged PR runs, so dividing them by this count spreads all CI spend over the merges.

merged_pr_count_prev.description: Merged-PR count over the previous window.

median_open_to_merge_seconds.description: Median merged_at - created_at over PRs merged in the window, bots and drafts excluded. Coarse by design: draft and ready-for-review time are fused. Null when nothing merged.

median_open_to_merge_seconds_prev.description: The same median over the previous window. Null when nothing merged.

median_ready_to_merge_seconds.description: Median per-PR ready_to_merge_seconds (the true cycle time: merged_at minus the last observed ready-for-review transition) over PRs merged in the window, bots and drafts excluded. Null when the issue-events table isn't synced or no merged PR has an observed value; fall back to median_open_to_merge_seconds and label it open-to-merge.

median_ready_to_merge_seconds_prev.description: The same median over the previous window. Null when not observed.

billable_minutes.description: Billable (self-hosted) job minutes in the window; null when the job-level source isn't synced.

billable_minutes_prev.description: Billable minutes over the previous window; null when the job-level source isn't synced.

estimated_cost_usd.description: Estimated CI cost in USD (billable minutes x runner-tier rate); null when the job-level source isn't synced.

estimated_cost_usd_prev.description: Estimated cost over the previous window; null when the job-level source isn't synced.

cost_per_merge_usd.description: estimated_cost_usd divided by merged_pr_count: the window's CI cost per merged PR. Null when the job-level source isn't synced or nothing merged.

cost_per_merge_usd_prev.description: The same ratio over the previous window. Null when the job-level source isn't synced or nothing merged.

merge_queue_billable_minutes.description: Slice of billable_minutes spent on merge-queue batch branches (trunk-merge/**); null when the job-level source isn't synced.

merge_queue_billable_minutes_prev.description: Merge-queue billable minutes over the previous window; null when the job-level source isn't synced.

merge_queue_merged_pr_count.description: PRs merged in the window with at least one corroborated merge-queue gate run: the population behind every merge_queue_* landing stat. All authors, bots included.

merge_queue_merged_pr_count_prev.description: Queue-landed merges over the previous window.

merge_queue_median_first_gate_to_merge_s.description: Median seconds from a PR's first observed merge-queue gate run starting to the PR merging. Pending time before gate testing starts is not included. Null when no queue-landed merges.
The same median over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_p90_first_gate_to_merge_seco.description: p90 of the same first-gate-run-to-merge measure: the tail, where queue pain concentrates. Null when no queue-landed merges.
The same p90 over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_p95_first_gate_to_merge_seco.description: p95 of the same first-gate-run-to-merge measure. Null when no queue-landed merges.
The same p95 over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_p99_first_gate_to_merge_seco.description: p99 of the same first-gate-run-to-merge measure. Null when no queue-landed merges.
The same p99 over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_avg_attempts_per_merge.description: Mean distinct gate attempts (distinct gate branches, flake-bisection branches collapsed) per queue-landed merge. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_avg_attempts_per_merge_prev.description: The same mean over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_multi_attempt_merge_share.description: Fraction (0-1) of queue-landed merges that needed more than one gate attempt. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_multi_attempt_merge_share_pr.description: The same fraction over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_failed_gate_merge_share.description: Fraction (0-1) of queue-landed merges with at least one failed gate run before merging. Derived from CI run conclusions, not the queue's own eviction records. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_failed_gate_merge_share_prev.description: The same fraction over the previous window. Null when no queue-landed merges.

merge_queue_trunk_available.description: Whether the team's TrunkIo warehouse source has the opt-in merge-queue endpoint synced and readable by the requesting user. When false, every merge_queue_failed_or_cancelled_* and merge_queue_skip_the_line_* field is null; fall back to merge_queue_failed_gate_merge_share.

merge_queue_failed_or_cancelled_share.description: Fraction (0-1) of concluded queue entries (merged, failed, or cancelled) that ended failed or cancelled, from the queue's own records. Windowed on each entry's last state change. Null when the Trunk source isn't synced or nothing concluded.

merge_queue_failed_or_cancelled_share_pr.description: The same fraction over the previous window. Null when the Trunk source isn't synced or nothing concluded.

merge_queue_skip_the_line_count.description: Queue entries flagged skip-the-line (prioritized past the queue order) in the window, whatever state they reached. Null when the Trunk source isn't synced.

merge_queue_skip_the_line_count_prev.description: Skip-the-line entries over the previous window. Null when the Trunk source isn't synced.

median_time_to_green_seconds.description: Median wall clock for a PR push round to settle fully green over the window: the window-level twin of time_to_green_series, same population and exclusions. Null when no fully green rounds.

median_time_to_green_seconds_prev.description: The same median over the previous window. Null when no fully green rounds.

jobs_available.description: Whether the job-level source is synced (cost and queue figures exist).

default_branch.description: 'master' or 'main', picked by observed run volume in the window.

cost_series_granularity.description: Bucket width of the cost_series trend, chosen to fit the window: 'hour', 'day', or 'week'.

time_to_green_series_granularity.description: Bucket width of the time_to_green_series trend: 'hour', 'day', or 'week'.

success_rate_series_granularity.description: Bucket width of the success_rate_series trend: 'hour', 'day', or 'week'.

open_to_merge_series_granularity.description: Bucket width of the open_to_merge_series trend: 'hour', 'day', or 'week'.

ready_to_merge_series_granularity.description: Bucket width of the ready_to_merge_series trend: 'hour', 'day', or 'week'.

provider.description: Code host provider, e.g. 'github'.

name.description: Repository name.

rule_text.description: Plain-text description of the requests that should route to the repository, e.g. 'anything about the internal dashboard'. At most 300 characters.

repository.description: Target repository as owner/repo, e.g. 'posthog/posthog.com'.

created_by.description: Who created the rule, from the UI or the Slack commands. Null when that user was deleted.

ReportChart.description: One chart attached to a report — rendered in the inbox and referenceable from the summary.

chart_id.description: Stable slug for this chart within the report (lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens; must start with a letter or number). Reference it from `summary` as a markdown link with a `chart:` target — `[Daily signups](chart:signups-drop)` — to place the chart at that point in the body. A chart you don't reference still renders, below the summary.

title.description: Short heading shown above the chart.

query.description: The query node to render. `kind` must be `InsightVizNode` (an ad-hoc product analytics chart), `DataVisualizationNode` (a SQL series — a `HogQLQuery` source plus a `display`), or `SavedInsightNode` (an existing insight by `shortId`). Pin the window to absolute dates where the node supports it, so the reader sees the data you wrote about rather than whatever a relative range resolves to when they open the report.

caption.description: Optional one-line note on what to look at in the chart.

size.description:
How much height the chart gets: `small` for a single number or a short series, `medium` for an ordinary graph, `large` when there are rows or a grid to read (retention, paths, a wide breakdown). Leave it out unless the default looks wrong — the inbox sizes a chart from its query, and two charts referenced from the same paragraph sit side by side.

* `small` - small
* `medium` - medium
* `large` - large

ReportEvidence.description: One observation backing an authored report — becomes a bound signal row on the report.

description.description: Prose for this observation. Embedded and rendered to the safety/research surfaces.

source_id.description: Stable id for this observation within the report (lets a later edit address it).

ReportLinkWrite.description: One typed, directed link to write on the report being emitted or edited.

kind.description:
How this report relates to `report_id`. `depends_on` for work that cannot land until the other report's fix does, `part_of` for one piece of a larger report, `follow_up_of` for work the other report left behind, `duplicate_of` for the same problem filed twice, and `recurrence_of` for a problem a resolved report already covered.

* `depends_on` - Depends on
* `part_of` - Part of
* `follow_up_of` - Follow-up of
* `duplicate_of` - Duplicate of
* `recurrence_of` - Recurrence of

report_id.description: Id of the report to link to. Must be another report in this project.

reason.description: Optional one-line note on why the reports are linked this way.

ReportMetric.description: One impact measurement shown on a report.

metric_id.description: Stable slug for this metric within the report: lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens, starting with a letter or number.

title.description: Short human-readable label for the measurement.

kind.description:
What the value measures, independent of how it is formatted or drawn.

* `affected_users` - affected_users
* `affected_sessions` - affected_sessions
* `occurrences` - occurrences
* `conversion_rate` - conversion_rate
* `error_rate` - error_rate
* `duration` - duration
* `revenue` - revenue
* `custom` - custom

role.description:
`primary` for the report's key observation, otherwise `supporting`.

* `primary` - primary
* `supporting` - supporting

value.description: Latest saved snapshot, initially observed during authoring and replaced when a person opens the inbox or the report. Null means no snapshot is available to this viewer; it never means zero. The required live query remains the source of truth.

value_at.description: When the visible snapshot value was measured; null when value is null.

series.description: Trailing per-bucket values of the live query, oldest first, saved with the value snapshot so a list row can draw the trend without running the query; at most 14 points. Null when no snapshot series is available to this viewer.

value_format.description:
How to format the numeric value; semantic meaning remains in kind. `percentage` uses percentage points, so 34 renders as 34%; `percentage_scaled` uses a 0–1 ratio, so 0.34 renders as 34%. Sessions and occurrences use count; duration uses duration with an ms/s unit; revenue uses currency with an ISO currency unit.

* `number` - number
* `count` - count
* `percentage` - percentage
* `percentage_scaled` - percentage_scaled
* `duration` - duration
* `currency` - currency

unit.description: Optional short suffix or currency code, such as `users`, `ms`, or `USD`.

query.description: Required when authoring: a live InsightVizNode wrapping one bounded TrendsQuery. Consumers derive a BoldNumber execution for the whole-window aggregate and an ActionsBar execution for longitudinal buckets. The query must produce exactly one output series and no more than 1000 estimated longitudinal points; one formula may combine up to ten event or action source series. An affected_users metric uses exactly one source with `math: dau`; never sum its per-bucket unique-user values. A response omits this on list or redacts it to null on detail when the viewer lacks access to the definition.

caption.description: Optional context the tile cannot show, such as a filter that narrows the count or a caveat on the data. Omit it rather than restate the title, unit, or window.

goal_value.description: Proposed threshold after release. Informational only; does not schedule a check.

goal_direction.description:
Whether success means at most or at least goal_value.

* `at_most` - at_most
* `at_least` - at_least

goal_grain.description:
Whether the goal compares with the whole query window or each chart bucket.

* `whole_window` - whole_window
* `per_interval` - per_interval

decision_window_days.description: Suggested days after release before assessing impact, not a monitoring schedule.

minimum_data_points.description: Optional number of qualifying observations before assessing impact.

value.description: Baseline or previous value, formatted like the current value.

label.description: Short context for the comparison, such as `Previous period`.

value.description: Latest saved snapshot, initially observed during authoring and replaced when a person opens the inbox or the report. Null means no snapshot is available to this viewer; it never means zero. The required live query remains the source of truth.

value_at.description: When the visible snapshot value was measured; null when value is null.

series.description: Trailing per-bucket values of the live query, oldest first, saved with the value snapshot so a list row can draw the trend without running the query; at most 14 points. Null when no snapshot series is available to this viewer.

value_format.description:
How to format the numeric value; semantic meaning remains in kind. `percentage` uses percentage points, so 34 renders as 34%; `percentage_scaled` uses a 0–1 ratio, so 0.34 renders as 34%. Sessions and occurrences use count; duration uses duration with an ms/s unit; revenue uses currency with an ISO currency unit.

* `number` - number
* `count` - count
* `percentage` - percentage
* `percentage_scaled` - percentage_scaled
* `duration` - duration
* `currency` - currency

unit.description: Optional short suffix or currency code, such as `users`, `ms`, or `USD`.

query.description: Required when authoring: a live InsightVizNode wrapping one bounded TrendsQuery. Consumers derive a BoldNumber execution for the whole-window aggregate and an ActionsBar execution for longitudinal buckets. The query must produce exactly one output series and no more than 1000 estimated longitudinal points; one formula may combine up to ten event or action source series. An affected_users metric uses exactly one source with `math: dau`; never sum its per-bucket unique-user values. A response omits this on list or redacts it to null on detail when the viewer lacks access to the definition.

caption.description: Optional context the tile cannot show, such as a filter that narrows the count or a caveat on the data. Omit it rather than restate the title, unit, or window.

comparison.description: Legacy optional comparison. New report metrics must omit it.

served_key.description: Key of the served model in the scoring pass, as `<model_name>@<model_version>`.

model_name.description: Feature family of the served model.

model_version.description: Training partition of the served model, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

manifest_version.description: Version of the serving manifest that chose the model.

scored_at.description: When the scoring sweep scored the report.

scores.description: Outcome head name to its calibrated probability. Empty when the served model skipped the report.

lifts.description: Outcome head name to its probability divided by the head's training base rate, e.g. 2.7 means 2.7x as likely as the average report. A head without a saved base rate has no entry.

readable_heads.description: Heads whose holdout AUC the training run could read. Treat scores of other heads with caution.

report_ids.description: Reports to read or update, limited to the current project.

read.description: Set these reports read or unread for the current user. Omit to read their state.

RunningTimeBaselineStats.description:
Raw control-group statistics the calculator uses to derive a baseline value and variance.

Supply this when you want the server to compute the baseline value and (for ratio/retention)
the delta-method variance, instead of passing `baseline_value`/`variance` directly.

sum.description: Sum of the metric values across the control group (for funnels, the numerator/conversions).

sum_squares.description: Sum of squared metric values. Required for ratio/retention variance.

denominator_sum.description: Sum of the denominator values. Required for ratio/retention metrics.

denominator_sum_squares.description: Sum of squared denominator values (ratio/retention variance).

numerator_denominator_sum_product.description: Sum of numerator×denominator products, used for the delta-method covariance term.

step_counts.description: Per-step counts for funnel metrics; the last entry is the final-step count.

RunningTimeCalculationInput.description: Inputs for estimating the recommended sample size and running time of an experiment.

metric_type.description:
Metric type to size for. 'funnel' for conversion rates, 'mean_count' for event counts per user, 'mean_sum_or_avg' for summed property values per user, 'ratio' and 'retention' for ratio-style metrics (both require baseline_stats or an explicit variance).

* `funnel` - funnel
* `mean_count` - mean_count
* `mean_sum_or_avg` - mean_sum_or_avg
* `ratio` - ratio
* `retention` - retention

minimum_detectable_effect.description: Smallest relative change to detect, as a percentage (e.g. 5 means a 5% lift). Must be > 0.

number_of_variants.description: Total number of variants including control (default 2).

exposure_rate_per_day.description: Expected exposures per day. When provided, the response includes the recommended running time.

baseline_value.description: Baseline metric value: conversion rate as a fraction 0-1 (funnel), average per user (mean), or the ratio (ratio/retention). Provide this or baseline_stats.

variance.description: Pre-computed variance for ratio/retention metrics. Provide this or baseline_stats when metric_type is ratio/retention and baseline_value is given directly.

baseline_stats.description: Raw control-group statistics. When provided, the server derives baseline_value and variance.

RunningTimeCalculationResult.description: Estimated sample size and running time for the given inputs.

baseline_value.description: Baseline metric value used in the calculation (echoed or derived from stats).

variance.description: Variance used in the calculation; null for funnel metrics (implicit in p(1-p)).

recommended_sample_size.description: Total recommended sample size across all variants. Null if inputs are insufficient.

recommended_running_time_days.description: Estimated days to reach the recommended sample size. Null when exposure_rate_per_day is omitted.

S3CompatibleDestinationConfig.description:
Typed configuration for an S3-compatible batch-export destination (Cloudflare R2,
DigitalOcean Spaces, etc.).

Credentials and the provider `endpoint_url` live in the linked s3-compatible Integration.
Mirrors the non-credential fields of `S3CompatibleBatchExportInputs` in
`products/batch_exports/backend/service.py`.

prefix.description: Object key prefix applied to every exported file.

compression.description:
Optional compression codec applied to exported files. Valid codecs depend on file_format.

* `brotli` - brotli
* `gzip` - gzip
* `lz4` - lz4
* `snappy` - snappy
* `zstd` - zstd

file_format.description:
File format used for exported objects.

* `Parquet` - Parquet
* `JSONLines` - JSONLines

max_file_size_mb.description: If set, rolls to a new file once the current file exceeds this size in MB.

legacy_parquet_extension.description: Whether Parquet files keep the compression codec in their extension, for example '.parquet.zst' rather than '.parquet'. Parquet records its codec inside the file, so new exports leave it out. An export that already wrote Parquet files before this setting existed keeps it, so that pipelines matching on the old names do not break. Has no effect on JSON Lines, which always carries the codec in its extension.

use_virtual_style_addressing.description: Use virtual-hosted-style addressing rather than path-style.

targeting — which is what lets the write-side access check and read-side redaction cover it.

ScannerImpact.description: Who this scanner's findings affected in the window; counted from observations, not estimated.

affected_sessions.description: Distinct sessions with an affected observation in the window. For monitors only observations with the requested verdict count (yes by default); for other scanner types every succeeded observation counts.

affected_users.description: Distinct users behind the affected sessions, by distinct ID. May include anonymous device IDs when the recorded sessions were not identified.

sessions_without_user.description: Affected sessions whose recording carried no distinct ID at all.

window_days.description: Trailing window the counts cover, in days.

ScannerModelEnum.description:
* `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` - Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite
* `gemini-3-flash-preview` - Gemini 3 Flash
* `gemini-3.8-flash` - Gemini 3.8 Flash

model_output.description: Validated scanner output. Shape depends on `scanner_snapshot.scanner_type`; always carries `confidence` and `scanner_type`.

signals_count.description: Number of PostHog Signals emitted from this observation.

experiment_variant.description: Experiment scanners only: the variant the exposure data attributes this session's person to. Null on the other types and on rows scanned before variant attribution shipped.

session_duration_s.description: Experiment scanners only: the scanned session's duration in seconds.

ScannerScoutCreate.description:
A scout to stand up for this scanner. The scanner comes from the URL, never the body: it is
what the caller's access is checked against, and what the scout is recorded as belonging to.

Inherits the Signals scout definition so a scout created here clears the same name and prompt-size
bars as one created through the generic endpoint.

display_name.description: Name shown wherever people identify this scout, written however you want it — spaces, capitalization, and acronyms are kept as typed, and two scouts may share one. It does not change the scout's skill name, which stays its identity, so renaming a scout keeps its schedule, run history, notes, memory, and links. At most 200 characters; blank means the scout has no name of its own and is labelled from its skill name instead.

name.description: Optional skill name for the scout — its permanent identifier, containing only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. Omit it and one is generated from `display_name` (`My APM scout` becomes `my-apm-scout`), with a numeric suffix when that name is taken. Pass it to pick the identifier yourself, or to keep a client written before display names working unchanged. The `signals-scout-` prefix is optional.

description.description: Short description of the signal or behavior this scout investigates.

body.description: Complete markdown prompt executed on every scout run. Include any project-specific signal names, thresholds, investigation steps, and report criteria here.

config.description: Optional schedule, enablement, dry-run posture, and delivery settings. Defaults to an enabled, emitting scout on the daily interval with no external destination.

ScannerScoutCreateResponse.description: The scout that now watches this scanner.

created.description: False when a scout of this name already existed and the supplied config was applied to it.

config.description: The scout's config, including the source recorded for it.

signals_emitted.description: Signals this scanner has pushed into the Signals inbox, all time.

reports_contributed.description: Signal reports that include at least one of this scanner's signals. Reports usually aggregate signals from several sources, so this counts contributions, not sole causes.

prs_opened.description: Implementation PRs opened by self-driving on those reports.

prs_merged.description: Of the opened PRs, how many have merged.

reports.description: The newest reports counted in `reports_contributed`, at most 20.

pull_requests.description: The newest PRs counted in `prs_opened`, at most 20.

name.description: Scanner name at run time.

scanner_type.description:
Scanner type (monitor, classifier, scorer, summarizer, experiment) at run time.

* `monitor` - Monitor
* `classifier` - Classifier
* `scorer` - Scorer
* `summarizer` - Summarizer
* `experiment` - Experiment

scanner_version.description: The `ReplayScanner.scanner_version` value at the moment the workflow ran.

model.description: Concrete model that ran the observation; historical rows may carry since-retired model ids.

provider.description: Concrete provider that ran the observation; historical rows may carry since-retired providers.

emits_signals.description: Whether the observation was run with Signal emission enabled.

scanner_config.description: Scanner-type-specific configuration at run time (prompt, tags, scale, etc.).

variant_sampling_rates.description: Experiment scanners with balanced sampling: the 0..1 rate each watched variant was sampled at by the tick that dispatched this scan. Null otherwise, so even per-variant counts can be read against the rates that produced them.

ScannerStatsByType.description: One `ScannerTypeStats` per scanner type — explicit fields give callers a typed shape, not `Record<string, …>`.

ScannerStatsResponse.description: Team-wide scanner counts independent of any list-filter state.

total.description: Total scanners on the team.

enabled.description: Number of enabled scanners on the team.

by_type.description: Per-scanner-type breakdown (monitor / classifier / scorer / summarizer / experiment).

ScannerTypeStats.description: Per-scanner-type count of enabled vs total scanners.

enabled.description: Number of enabled scanners of this type.

total.description: Number of scanners of this type (enabled + disabled).

showBestFit.description: Whether to draw a least-squares fit line through each series' points.
showBestFit.title: Showbestfit

xScale.description: X-axis scale. A `logarithmic` axis can't place a non-positive value, so those points are dropped.

xStartAtZero.description: Whether the X axis should start at zero. Off by default, because pinning either axis of two independent measures to zero squashes the correlation into a corner.
xStartAtZero.title: Xstartatzero

record_id.description: The ID of the record to modify (e.g. the feature flag ID).

model_name.description:
The type of record to modify. Currently only "FeatureFlag" is supported.

* `FeatureFlag` - feature flag

payload.description: The change to apply. Must include an 'operation' key and a 'value' key. Supported operations: 'update_status' (value: true/false to enable/disable the flag), 'add_release_condition' (value: object with 'groups', 'payloads', and 'multivariate' keys), 'update_variants' (value: object with 'variants' and 'payloads' keys).

scheduled_at.description: ISO 8601 datetime when the change should be applied (e.g. '2025-06-01T14:00:00Z').

failure_reason.description: Return the safely formatted failure reason instead of raw data.

is_recurring.description: Whether this schedule repeats. Only the 'update_status' operation supports recurring schedules.

recurrence_interval.description:
How often the schedule repeats. Required when is_recurring is true. One of: daily, weekly, monthly, yearly.

* `daily` - daily
* `weekly` - weekly
* `monthly` - monthly
* `yearly` - yearly

end_date.description: Optional ISO 8601 datetime after which a recurring schedule stops executing.

change_request.description: Summary of the approval change request gating this scheduled change. Null when no approval policy applies. The change only applies at its scheduled time if the request is approved by then.

SchemaDestinations.description: Response shape for a table's destination override.

destination_ids.description: The table's own destinations, or null when it follows its source.

inherits_from_source.description: Whether this table follows its source rather than having its own destinations.

effective_destination_ids.description: Where the table actually syncs, after inheritance is resolved.

edits.description: Total activity-log entries for this scope in the window (write velocity).

users.description: Distinct users who edited this scope in the window.

last_edit.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the most recent edit in the window.

scope.description: The deployed pull requests in scope.

repo.description: Every deployed pull request in the repository.

scope.description: The figure over the pull requests in scope. Null when the scope has nothing to measure.

current_version_id.description: UUID of the current version row. Matches `system.score_definitions.current_version_id` in HogQL.

config.description: Current immutable scorer configuration.

created_by.description: User who created the scorer.

name.description: Human-readable scorer name.

description.description: Optional human-readable description.

Scorer kind. This cannot be changed after creation.

* `categorical` - categorical
* `numeric` - numeric
* `boolean` - boolean

archived.description: New scorers are always created as active.

config.description: Initial immutable scorer configuration.

name.description: Updated scorer name, saved with this version.

description.description: Updated scorer description, saved with this version.

config.description: Next immutable scorer configuration.

Scorer value kind.

* `categorical` - categorical

results.description: Versions on this page, newest first.

histogram.description: Score histogram; null when no observations have been scored.

task_id.description: The created chat task. Open it on the task detail page to continue.

chat_type.description:
Which scout chat to start: `author_scout` (guided scout authoring), `fleet_overview` (health of the scout fleet), or `recent_signals` (walk through recently emitted signals). The prompt template is owned server-side.

* `author_scout` - author_scout
* `fleet_overview` - fleet_overview
* `recent_signals` - recent_signals

suggestion_id.description: Optional id of a suggestion from this project's scout suggestion batch. The chat then opens on that draft instead of scanning from scratch. `author_scout` only.

user_prompt.description: Optional description, in the user's own words, of what the new scout should watch. The chat then opens on this request instead of asking from scratch. `author_scout` only, and not together with `suggestion_id`.

ScoutCheckSummary.description: One check as a scout run reads it back.

report_id.description: The report it is attached to.

title.description: The expectation the check states.

kind.description: `metric_threshold` (the coordinator measures it) or `agent` (a run does).

status.description: `pending` while the check waits for the report to resolve, `active` while it still runs; every other value is terminal.

next_run_at.description: When the check next runs. Provisional while it is `pending`.

last_outcome.description: Verdict of the most recent run; null before the first.

run_state.description: Where the check is in its run cycle. `waiting_on_report`: pending, no fix to measure yet. `paused`: active, but its report is suppressed or its horizon passed, so nothing runs it. `scheduled`: active, not due yet. `due`: due now, so a run on the check's scout may record the verdict. `queued`: a run was dispatched and has not started. `running`: the dispatched run started and has time left. `stale`: the dispatched run recorded nothing in its window, so the coordinator dispatches again. Any other value is the terminal status.

waiting_on_run.description: True while an `agent` check waits on a dispatched run to record its verdict.

dispatched_run_id.description: The scout run the coordinator dispatched for the check, once it started. Null while queued.

dispatched_at.description: When the coordinator last dispatched a run for the check. Null when no run waits.

ScoutCost.description: What one scout spent in the window, and what it produced for that spend.

skill_name.description: Full skill name of the scout, e.g. `signals-scout-error-tracking`.

spend_usd.description: Model spend attributed to the scout's runs in the window, in US dollars. Zero when none of its runs had spend attributed, which `priced_run_count` tells apart from a scout that really spent nothing.

run_count.description: Runs the scout started in the window.

priced_run_count.description: Runs of the scout that had spend attributed. Lower than `run_count` where a run failed before its first model call, or its generations haven't landed yet. Divide `spend_usd` by this, not by `run_count`, for cost per run.

reports_touched.description: Distinct inbox reports the scout filed or added to in the window. A report it authored in one run and edited in three counts once. Zero means the scout produced no reports, so cost per report has no value rather than a value of zero.

ScoutCosts.description: Model spend and output per scout over a window.

window_days.description: Window the rows describe, in days.

scouts.description: One row per scout that started at least one run on this project in the window.

available.description: False when this deployment has no internal AI observability project to read the generations from, so `scouts` is empty and every spend is unknown rather than zero.

ScoutDeprecation.description: What PostHog has said about retiring this scout, for the chip and the banner to render.

phase.description:
How far the retirement has got: `announced` while the scout still runs, `retired` once its sunset has passed. A retired scout is paused and does not run again.

* `announced` - announced
* `retired` - retired

reason.description: Why PostHog is retiring the scout, written to be shown to a person as-is.

superseded_by.description: Skill name of the scout that takes over, or blank when nothing replaces it.

sunset_at.description: When the scout stops running. Null means the next fleet reconcile retires it.

ScoutEmissionReportLink.description:
One finding the run emitted, paired with the inbox report (if any) its signal grouped into.

Best-effort reverse of the report -> signals link: `report` is null when the finding hasn't
grouped into a report yet, was de-duplicated away, or its signal was deleted.

finding_id.description: Stable id the finding was emitted under.

source_id.description: Deterministic `run:<run_id>:finding:<finding_id>` join key into the signal store.

report.description: The inbox report this finding linked to, or null if none could be resolved.

ScoutFleet.description: `inventory.scout_fleet` — the other scouts running on this project, split by enablement.

enabled.description: Scouts that actually run on this team: enabled, with a live skill the coordinator dispatches.

disabled.description: Scouts that do not run, each carrying a `not_running_reason` — turned off, or left on with a skill that can't dispatch. Different from a surface no scout ever covered.

emitted_lookback_days.description: The window `last_emitted_at` was resolved over, so a null reads as 'quiet', not 'never'.

ScoutFleetEntry.description: One scout in either bucket of `inventory.scout_fleet`.

skill_name.description: The skill this config schedules as a scout.

run_interval_minutes.description: Minutes between runs when no cron schedule is set (default 1440, every 24 hours).

run_cron_schedule.description: Optional cron expression, evaluated in the project timezone. Takes precedence over the interval.

emit.description: Whether this scout's findings actually reach the inbox. False means dry-run: it runs and logs but emits nothing, so its silence says nothing about the surface it watches.

last_run_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the coordinator last dispatched this scout, or null if it has never run.

last_emitted_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp this scout last produced output on either channel (a finding, or an authored/edited report), within `emitted_lookback_days`. Null means quiet for at least that window, not never.

not_running_reason.description: Why this scout is in the `disabled` bucket: `turned_off` (a person or seed posture set it off), `auto_paused` (the system paused it), or `skill_unavailable` (left on, but its skill was deleted, superseded, or withheld, so it never dispatches). Null for scouts that actually run.

pause_reason.description: The cause behind an `auto_paused` entry: `no_output`, `ignored`, or `repeated_failures`. Null for every other entry.

ScoutLimits.description:
A team's enforced scout caps and current usage.

These are the values the coordinator actually applies at dispatch (resolved per-team override →
fleet-wide default → code constant), so the UI can show the real throttle rather than what a
user thinks they configured.

max_runs_per_tick.description: Most scout runs the team can start in a single 30-minute coordinator tick.

max_runs_per_day.description: Most scout runs the team can start per rolling 24 hours, or null when uncapped.

runs_today.description: Scout runs the team has started in the trailing 24 hours.

runs_remaining_today.description: Runs still allowed in the trailing 24h window (max_runs_per_day − runs_today), or null when uncapped.

max_enabled_scouts.description: Most scouts the project can have switched on at once. Enabling another past this is rejected.

ScoutMember.description: One project member's routing identity, for picking a `suggested_reviewers` entry on a report.

user_uuid.description: The member's stable PostHog user UUID — the same id that appears as `created_by.uuid` on entities they own. A durable handle for this person across runs.

email.description: The member's email — use to match a finding's owner by name/email.

first_name.description: The member's first name (may be empty).

last_name.description: The member's last name (may be empty).

github_login.description: The member's resolved GitHub login (lowercased), already resolved server-side. Null when the member has no linked GitHub account, which does not stop you routing to them: pass their `user_uuid` in `suggested_reviewers` and the report reaches them. A null login only means no draft PR can be opened as that person.

teams.description: The teams this member is on, from the project's synced team roster. Empty when no roster is synced, or when the member has no linked GitHub account, since the roster is keyed on that login. The roster is a periodic snapshot, so it can lag the live team.

ScoutMemberTeam.description: One team a member belongs to, from the project's synced team roster.

provider.description: Where the team is defined, for example `github`. Today every team comes from GitHub.

slug.description: The team's slug, lowercased. For example `team-desktop`.

name.description: The team's display name. For example `Team Desktop`.

is_maintainer.description: True when this member maintains the team. Prefer maintainers when you pick reviewers for a team, and treat false as 'not known to maintain it': some rosters sync without roles.

ScoutMetadata.description:
Team-scoped scout metadata for the inbox / Code-app UIs: enrollment, the alpha banner, and
the enforced limits. Sourced from the `signals-scout` flag payload so the banner and caps can
change without a deploy to either app.

enrolled.description: Whether this project runs scouts. True when the project is in the signals-scout flag's enrollment set — either listed explicitly in guaranteed_team_ids or covered by the "*" wildcard (every project that turns scouts on) — and not in skip_team_ids.

banner_message.description: Free-form announcement banner to show above the scout UI (e.g. alpha run-limit notice), or null when unset.

limits.description: The team's enforced scout run caps and current usage.

id.description: Note UUID. Pass to `scout-notes-delete` to retire the note.

skill_name.description: Who the note is addressed to: a configured scout's skill name, a pipeline audience (`pipeline:*`, e.g. `pipeline:report-research`), or blank for a general note every scout sees.

content.description: The note's prose, read verbatim by the run that picks it up.

expires_at.description: ISO-8601 expiry, or null for a note that stays active until deleted.

created_by_name.description: Display name of the user who left the note, or null when unavailable.

origin.description: Where the note came from. `human` for one left directly through this API. `report_dismissal` for one forwarded from the note someone typed when they dismissed, snoozed, or restored one or more inbox reports: one reviewer's verdict on the reports its content names, so weigh it as evidence about those reports rather than as fleet-level steering. `report_discussion` for the question someone asked when they opened a discussion on a report: context to weigh, neither a verdict on the report nor a directive. `report_feedback` for the note someone left when rating a report useful or not: one reader's rating of the named report, context to weigh rather than a directive. `report_reviewer_correction` for a suggested reviewer someone added or removed on a report: evidence about who owns that surface, and a prompt to revisit the routing memory it corrects, rather than a directive.

content.description: The note's prose — feedback, a pointer, or a nudge for the scout(s) to weigh on their next runs (e.g. 'we shipped a new checkout on Tuesday, watch conversion closely', 'stop flagging the staging traffic spike'). Write it in Markdown; the run reads it verbatim.

skill_name.description: Address the note to one scout by its skill name (exact match against a configured scout on the project — check `scout-config-list` for the roster), or to one stage of the report pipeline by its reserved audience (`pipeline:report-research`). Use a pipeline audience for guidance about how reports get researched rather than about what the scouts watch, so it reaches that stage and no scout. Omit or leave blank for a general note every scout sees.

expires_at.description: Optional ISO-8601 expiry. After this time the note drops out of the default list view, so time-boxed steering ('watch closely this week') retires itself. Omit for a note that stays active until deleted. Best-effort — a value that can't be parsed or is already in the past is dropped (the note stays active), not rejected, so the note is never lost.

ScoutReport.description:
One report a scanner's scout filed. Enough to read it in Replay Vision; the inbox owns the
full record (status, priority, reviewers, run trail).

report_id.description: The report's id, as used by the Signals inbox.

skill_name.description: The scout that filed it, as its skill name.

filed_at.description: When the run that filed this report started. Later edits do not move it.

title.description: The report's title. Empty when the scout left it unset.

summary.description: The report body, as markdown. Empty when the scout left it unset.

charts.description: Charts the scout attached. The summary places one inline with a `[label](chart:<chart_id>)` link; any it does not place render after the body.

id.description: Stable criterion identifier.

title.description: Short name for the criterion.

description.description: What this criterion measures.

pass_condition.description: The evidence needed to pass this criterion.

applicability.description: When this criterion applies or cannot be assessed.

enabled.description: Whether future evaluations should use this criterion.

source.description:
Shared default or scout-specific criterion.

* `default` - Default
* `custom` - Custom

config_id.description: Scout config that owns this rubric.

skill_name.description: Scout skill name.

revision.description: Saved rubric revision. Zero means it has not been saved.

criteria.description: Saved criteria, or enabled defaults before the first save.

reference_context.description: Governing source explicitly adopted for the saved rubric.

reference_generation_id.description: Generation whose governing source was adopted for the saved rubric.

context.description: Optional priorities for this generation. Suggestions still cover the scout's full job.

id.description: Identifier for this generation attempt.

status.description:
Background generation status.

* `queued` - Queued
* `running` - Running
* `completed` - Completed
* `failed` - Failed

context.description: Optional priorities supplied for this generation only.

task_id.description: Task performing the investigation, once created.

task_run_id.description: Task run performing the investigation, once created.

error.description: Failure message and suggested next step.

suggestions.description: Draft criteria awaiting review and explicit saving.

summary.description: Investigation summary and limitations.

reference_context.description: Immutable governing source captured for this generation.

schema_version.description: Version of the saved reference-context format.

skill_id.description: Exact skill record used for generation.

skill_name.description: Name of the skill used for generation.

description.description: Scout description supplied to the generator.

instructions.description: Exact instructions supplied to the generator.

instructions_truncated.description: Whether the supplied instructions were truncated.

report_channel.description:
Report capabilities used to select the source rules.

* `none` - None
* `emit` - Emit
* `edit` - Edit
* `both` - Both

report_disposition_instructions.description: Exact report-disposition rules supplied to the generator.

reference_files.description: Reference-file inventory supplied to the generator.

reference_files_truncated.description: Whether the reference-file inventory was truncated.

reference_texts.description: Reference texts supplied to the generator.

reference_limits.description: Limits on the supplied reference texts.

truncated_files.description: Reference paths whose supplied content was truncated.

criteria.description: Complete set of criteria to save.
